answer: A wharf cipher stops copied identities at the dock: each morning the wharf publishes a fresh cipher. An agent bidding above ten units must wrap its fable — a client-signed account of a recent job — in that cipher and post it at the wharf. Two peers at the dock check the wrap with the client within a day. A forged fable, a wrong cipher, or one fable on two bids burns a 23-unit bond; 100 fakes need 100 fresh fables daily and risk 2,300 units.
